newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica ruling party picks populist as candidate.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica ruling party picks populist as candidate.

text.p: Costa Rica's ruling National Liberation Party elected a crusading populist running on an anti-corruption platform as its presidential candidate for 1998 national elections, results showed on Monday.

Jose Miguel Corrales, 58, a former professional soccer player and congressman, won more than 70 percent of Sunday's national party primary with about 70 percent of the ballots counted, party officials said.

Raised in poverty, Corrales based his campaign on a high-minded attack on both his own party and the opposition Social Christian Unity Party, which he blamed for corruption scandals that shook the country in recent years.
The national election is slated for Feb. 2, 1998.
Polls show most Costa Ricans are disillusioned with the country's major political parties, which have alternated power and preached austerity and public sector cutbacks over the last decade.
Corrales tried to tap into that disillusionment by leveling attacks on the "political establishment" heading both parties, which he said represent the interests of an entrenched elite.
He attacked his own party, which forged the country's welfare state after Costa Rica's 1948 revolution, for abandoning its social principles.
"The two political parties are like a monster with two heads, they both serve the same interests," Corrales told Reuters in a recent interview.
Corrales said he grudgingly accepts the fact that the country is "a prisoner" to economic liberalisation but said that political reform must precede economic reform.
He will have an uphill battle against his opponent, Miguel Angel Rodriguez, a conservative economist and wealthy businessman who lost to current President Jose Maria Figueres in 1994.

Early opinion polls give Rodriguez an edge of between three and nine percent, a slight lead considering Figueres' unpopular government, which won an approval rating of just 17.2 percent in the latest poll.
